name: Athena street-crime risk model

evaluation.baseline_description: predicts risk from last month's crime count alone

bands.high: predicted risk in the top 5% of scored segments (cut at 0.6375) AND >= 2 street crimes recorded in the last 90 days
bands.medium: predicted risk at/above the 75th percentile (cut at 0.0301) AND >= 1 street crime in the last 90 days
bands.low: everything else -- including streets whose only incidents are months old
bands.note: both model risk AND real recent Police UK records are required for high/medium: a street with an old incident cluster and clean recent months cannot be rated high, no matter how the percentile falls

recency_handling.formula: sum over prior months of count * 0.5^(k/1.5); half-life 1.5 months, so a 3-month-old incident weighs a quarter of a fresh one
recency_handling.combined_with: log1p_lag1/log1p_lag2 (last two months) -- fresh activity always dominates
recency_handling.window_note: decay is computed over the fetched Police UK window (2026-02..2026-08); incidents older than the window are invisible (they drop out, not decay gradually)

removed_features.reason: moved to router as preference multiplier
removed_features.detail: lighting encodes the user's well-lit-roads preference, not crime causation; kept in the model it confounds preference with prediction

removed_features.reason: moved to router as preference multiplier
removed_features.detail: as lit_no; also a near-empty dummy in this dataset

removed_features.reason: moved to router as preference multiplier
removed_features.detail: unknown-lighting segments are never scored at all (honesty rule), so the dummy carries no signal

removed_features.reason: moved to router as preference multiplier
removed_features.detail: quiet-vs-busy streets are a route preference the user can weigh, not a crime predictor we should bake in
riverside exposure is rare in the crime window and the fitted weight is negligible; live tide data is shown in the app instead
safe-haven density tracks the city centre and duplicates log_dist_centre (confounded); havens are surfaced on the map, not in the crime score

design_choice: Preference-related attributes (lighting, isolation, tide exposure, haven proximity, terrain) are separated from crime prediction so a user's preferences cannot bias the risk estimate: the model predicts reported street crime only, and the router applies each user's preferences as explicit edge-cost multipliers. Bands are percentile-calibrated (75th/95th percentile of the fit's scored predictions) AND gated on real recent incidents, so a high badge always reflects both the model and current Police UK records. Incident recency decays exponentially (half-life 1.5 months) inside log1p_decay.
known_limitations: Time-of-day gap: Police UK street-level data has no time field, so the model predicts reported street crime generally, not night-time crime specifically; the night framing is carried by the router's preferences (lighting, quiet streets), not by data.
Crime-location blurring: Police UK snaps crimes to an anonymous nearby street point; we snap to the nearest walking segment within 120 m, so segment-level counts are approximate by construction.

Lag-feature dominance: recent-crime history (log1p_lag1 coefficient 0.2734) is the strongest signal; where a street has no recent records the model falls back on structure (type, length, centre distance) and is correspondingly less certain.
Unknown-lighting exclusion: 45% of walking segments have no lighting data in OSM and are never scored; they show as grey 'risk unknown' in the app rather than being silently guessed.
Decay window: the recency decay spans the Police UK fetch window (2026-02..2026-08); incidents older than the window are invisible to the model (they drop out, not decay gradually).
